message.content: In lions, one of the most noticeable dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult male individuals. The genes responsible for mane growth are expressed dominantly, so a single copy of the relevant allele is sufficient for the mane to develop. This trait is often used as a classic example of dominance in mammalian genetics.
